image_description: A high-angle, close-up shot of a Nile crocodile partially submerged in murky brown water. The view focuses on the dorsal surface of the head and upper back, showcasing the rough, armored texture of the skin and the prominent bony ridges (osteoderms) running down the spine. The snout is visible at the bottom, tapering into the water, while the top of the head shows the characteristic eye bumps.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the snout tapers to a point consistent with the V-shape of a crocodile, distinct from the U-shape of an alligator.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and the jawline is largely submerged or obscured by the angle; individual teeth are not clearly visible for verification.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the orbital ridges are visible, the eyes themselves are either closed, covered by water glare, or angled away, making pupil shape and membrane visibility impossible to verify.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The very tip of the snout is submerged or cut off by the frame edge; nostrils are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible section of the body extending from the neck shows heavy armor plating and continues out of frame, implying an elongated structure typical of the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays two prominent parallel rows of raised bony scutes running down the center of the back, matching the anatomical description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of muddy browns and greys, and the texture is visibly rough, knobby, and calcified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a dorsal (top-down) view; the belly/ventral side is completely occluded by the body and water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No limbs are visible in this specific crop; they are either underwater or outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is not visible in the frame.

While many checkpoints were untestable due to the tight, dorsal-only framing, there are no contradictions in the visible anatomy. The texture and lighting are realistic.
